definitions.explanation: the degree to which something allows light to pass through, or figuratively, how open and clear something is

examples.japanese: この{湖|みずうみ}は{透明度|とうめいど}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This lake has high water clarity.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}の{透明度|とうめいど}は{天候|てんこう}によって{変|か}わる。
examples.english: The transparency of the sea changes depending on the weather.

examples.japanese: {沖縄|おきなわ}の{海|うみ}は{透明度|とうめいど}が{高|たか}く、{海底|かいてい}まで{見通|みとお}せるほどだ。
examples.english: The sea in Okinawa is so clear that you can see all the way to the ocean floor.

notes:
Composed of {透明|とうめい} (transparent, clear) + {度|ど} (degree). Most commonly used to describe the clarity of water in lakes, oceans, and rivers. Also used figuratively for organizational transparency.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {透明度|とうめいど}が{高|たか}い: high transparency/clarity
- {透明度|とうめいど}が{低|ひく}い: low transparency
- {透明度|とうめいど}を{測|はか}る: to measure transparency
- {水|みず}の{透明度|とうめいど}: water clarity
- {透明度|とうめいど}が{落|お}ちる: transparency decreases

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {透明|とうめい}: transparent, clear — the base adjective describing the property itself
- {透明性|とうめいせい}: transparency — used more abstractly for organizational/political transparency
- {濁|にご}り: turbidity, murkiness — the opposite quality
